cause_quote: The new resolver's probe accepted any non-Bun node: `process.stdout.write(!process.versions.bun&&(!requiredFlag||process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags.has(requiredFlag))?process.execPath:"")`, with no supported-version check, so the first Node on PATH won even if unsupported.
user_saw: When OpenClaw ran under Bun with an old Node (e.g. 20) earlier on PATH than a supported one, Node helper subprocesses such as Gateway post-ready maintenance crashed with a syntax error on `using` declarations.
summary: The Node helper-runtime resolver (fast path and standalone probe) now also requires the candidate Node to satisfy the canonical supported-version predicate.
reasoning: resolveNodeRuntimeExecutable was introduced in #145688 to find a real Node under Bun, and both its fast path and probe only excluded Bun and checked a flag, never the Node version; later commits (#183120, #183493) moved the probe into a generated asset without changing the predicate. The defect therefore shipped with the resolver; medium confidence because it only bites once helper code uses syntax the stray old Node lacks, which could be read as latent.
